blurb:
One year old, five pounds, and ready for a home. Harley is a domestic shorthair who is already litterbox trained and gets along with other animals, which at her age means she's had enough experience with the world to figure out how to share space. That's not nothing.

She's fully vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and flea-treated. The shelter doesn't have notes yet on how she does with kids, so if you've got little ones at home, ask when you visit. The staff can point you in the right direction or set up an introduction to see how she responds.

Harley is one of those cats where the basics are already handled. She knows what a litterbox is for, she's not going to terrorize your other pets, and she's young enough to adapt quickly to a new routine. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours and ask to meet her.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• A young, litterbox trained, animal-compatible cat with full vetting is about as turnkey as cat adoption gets, appealing to first-timers and experienced owners alike
• The blurb is competent but lacks a hook — no backstory or distinctive trait elevates her above a standard profile
• No urgency cues or long-stay language suggest a relatively recent arrival, reducing the emotional pressure to act now

blurb:
Four months old and already a full five pounds. Davie is a domestic shorthair kitten who is somehow already litterbox trained and gets along with other animals, which at her age is honestly impressive. A lot of kittens are chaos on four legs at this stage. Davie seems to have skipped that phase, or at least she's already working through it.

She's vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and flea-treated, so she's ready to go the day you decide she's coming home. The shelter doesn't have notes yet on how she does with kids, so if that matters to your household, it's worth asking when you visit. The staff can walk you through it.

If you've been thinking about adding a cat and wanted one young enough to really settle into your home and grow with your family, Davie is worth a visit. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Stop in during visiting hours and ask to meet her.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Kitten who is already litterbox trained and animal-friendly is a rare, high-appeal adoption candidate for a wide range of households
• Straightforward profile lacks a dramatic backstory but her above-average maturity for her age is a genuinely charming angle
• Language suggests a recent intake with no urgency signals, meaning she likely hasn't been waiting long and may move quickly on her own

blurb:
She came in with a name that tells you something about her. Momma is a one-year-old domestic medium hair who weighs just over six pounds, which means she's small but has clearly already done some living. She's been through enough to earn that name, and now she's ready for a quieter chapter.

She's litterbox trained and fully vetted — vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and flea-treated. The shelter doesn't have a full picture yet of how she does with other animals or kids, which makes sense given where she's coming from. If you've got other pets, ask the staff about a meet and greet before committing. They'll work with you.

What she needs is someone patient. Someone who's willing to let her figure out that she's safe now. That kind of trust takes a little time, but it's worth it. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours and ask for Momma.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Her name and implied backstory create instant emotional pull for newsletter readers seeking a meaningful adoption
• Fully vetted and litterbox trained lowers practical barriers, but the need for patience may narrow the ideal adopter pool
• Unknown compatibility with animals and kids suggests she's still settling in, hinting at a moderate shelter stay worth highlighting

blurb:
Victor wags with his whole body. Not just the tail. The whole body. That's the thing the volunteers keep coming back to when they describe him, and it's a pretty good summary of who this dog is. He's a five-year-old bulldog mix, 44 pounds, and apparently so happy to spend time with people that he once sat completely still through a bath just soaking up the one-on-one attention. His foster turns the TV on for him when he leaves the house. Victor, it seems, has fully settled into being loved.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's been worked with and knows what's expected of him. He does get mouthy and excited when things get rowdy, so kids 15 and up are the better fit. He also prefers being the only dog in the house. He's been through the training, but he's still got a strong personality and some strength behind it.

One more thing worth knowing: his foster is currently helping him work through some leg challenges, so check the medical notes on his profile page before reaching out. The team at Mostly Mutts will walk you through where he stands.

Victor is in a foster home and ready to meet his people. Head to the Mostly Mutts website to submit an inquiry and go from there.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Whole-body wag and 'foster turns the TV on for him' are vivid, personality-forward details that create instant affection in readers
• Stacked placement restrictions—only dog, older teens, active leg challenges—make him a compelling but difficult feature requiring careful framing
• Ongoing medical situation and single-dog preference suggest he has been waiting and will continue to wait without a well-targeted spotlight

blurb:
Eleven years old and still has a spring in his step. Meeko is a 33-pound Jack Russell/Greyhound mix who came out of animal control and landed in a foster home where he has apparently been thriving ever since. He climbs right into laps. He makes grateful little sighs during baths. He is, by every available measure, a good boy who knows he got lucky and is very happy about it.

He's got some opinions, which honestly feels appropriate for a dog who's been around this long. He wants to be your only dog, not because he's aggressive, but just because that's where he's most comfortable. He'll ignore the neighbor's big dogs from across the yard without a second thought, he just doesn't want to share a household. He can also get vocal when he wants attention, so a house with some space is a better fit than a condo or apartment.

Kids 15 and up are a good match. He got a little nervous around younger kids during his meet and greet at the shelter, so he'd do best in a quieter home. But if you're looking for a calm, affectionate, slightly spunky dog to sit with you in the evenings, Meeko is genuinely hard to beat.

He's currently in a foster home through Mostly Mutts. Submit an inquiry on their website to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Animal control origin plus 'grateful little sighs during baths' is the kind of specific, tender detail that makes newsletter readers fall in love immediately
• Eleven-year-old single-dog-only placement with older-teen household requirement makes him statistically hard to place, raising feature urgency
• Senior Jack Russell/Greyhound mix from AC with multiple household restrictions strongly implies a longer road to adoption

blurb:
Nine years old, 64 pounds, and somehow still the goofiest dog in the room. Bolton is a hound/boxer mix who came to Mostly Mutts underweight and rough around the edges, but you'd never know it now. His foster says he lights up every room he walks into, and that tracks. This is a dog who plays tag with other dogs by sprinting toward them and then bolting the other way, just hoping they'll chase him. He's been through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's not just charming, he's got some skills to back it up.

His energy is the best kind of senior energy. He'll sniff every inch of a trail with full hound commitment, then come home and happily park himself next to you on the couch. No drama. Just a sweet, loyal dog who had a hard start and is clearly grateful for the second chance.

A couple things to know: no cats, since he'll chase them. He's been great with kids around 8 to 12 in his foster home, but toddlers would be a tough fit since he's a big guy and could accidentally knock them over. Dogs are fine, he actually loves greeting them on walks. If you've got a dog-friendly house and a couch with room for one more, Bolton is worth meeting.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can browse adoptable dogs and submit an inquiry directly through their website.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Senior dog who came in underweight and transformed through care is a high-emotion, high-shareability narrative for newsletter readers
• Prison Pups training credential adds credibility and distinguishes him from untrained senior dogs who are harder to place
• Nine-year-old hound mix with cat restriction signals a harder-to-place profile, implying meaningful time in the system

blurb:
Pumps is the shyest one of the litter, and her foster will tell you that upfront. She's two and a half months old, part of the shoe-themed sibling group at Mostly Mutts, and she takes the longest to warm up of the bunch. If you walk in expecting a kitten to run straight at you, that's not her. She's going to watch you from a safe spot first and make sure you're worth the effort.

Here's the thing though. She's also curious about everything. She wants to know what's happening, who you are, and what that thing in your hand is. She just prefers to figure it out on her own timeline. Once she decides you're okay, the foster says she turns playful and adventurous. Chasing toys, wrestling with her siblings, finding the best high spots in the room. She's a real kitten underneath the caution, she just needs a patient person to draw it out.

She recently moved to the Kitty Room at the shelter, so you can go meet her in person now. She'd do best in a quieter home with adults or older, gentle kids. No rough handling and no sudden movements. If you have another calm cat at home, that could actually help her settle in faster.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Head to mostlymutts.org to start the process or stop in during adoption hours to say hello.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• Shyest of the litter with the most placement constraints narrows the adopter pool and reduces newsletter urgency
• The 'patient person will unlock her' narrative has charm but is the least differentiated story of the shoe-themed siblings
• Recent move to the Kitty Room suggests she is newly available rather than long-waiting, limiting time-based urgency

blurb:
He's two and a half months old, weighs about two pounds, and his name is Loafer. The shoe theme alone makes him worth a visit, but the personality is what's going to get you.

Loafer is part of a litter that was born right into the Mostly Mutts program and has been growing up in a foster home since day one. His foster mom calls them a great group of kittens, and Loafer fits that description. He's a little shy when you first meet him, the kind of shy where he'll hang back and watch you from across the room before deciding you're worth investigating. But curious doesn't even cover it. He wants to know what's going on at all times. Give him a few minutes to figure you out, and he opens right up.

He loves playtime, chasing toys, wrestling with his siblings, and climbing whatever he can get his paws on. He's litter trained, which is a nice bonus at this age. He also gets along with the ferret in his foster home, which honestly just adds to the charm.

He'd do best with older, gentle kids since sudden movements still startle him a bit. And if you already have a cat at home who might enjoy a small chaotic roommate, Loafer would probably love that too.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Visit mostlymutts.org to start the adoption process or come meet him in person.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• Kitten appeal is peak newsletter clickbait—tiny, named after a shoe, lives with a ferret, easy placement potential
• Shy-but-curious arc gives readers a feel-good adoption fantasy with low perceived difficulty
• Born into the program and still very young, suggesting minimal shelter time and low urgency for featured placement

blurb:
There's a lot of backstory packed into six pounds of tuxedo cat. Boots came into Mostly Mutts after a family member passed away and a good neighbor stepped in to care for her. She was pregnant when she arrived, went straight to a foster home, and raised four kittens there. Some of those babies already have homes now. Boots is next, and she has earned it.

She's an independent girl, which means she's not going to follow you room to room demanding attention. She does her own thing, and when she's ready for company, she'll find you. Comes over for pets, sits in your lap for a while, then goes back to her spot. If you've ever had a cat who respected your personal space while also expecting you to respect hers, you already know this personality type and you probably loved it.

One thing to know: she can get overstimulated during petting and will give a little nip to let you know she's done. Not aggressive, just communicating. Her foster figured out her signals quickly and says they get along great. She'd do best with adults or older kids who understand cat body language and won't push past her limits.

She gets along well with other cats and is litter trained. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw, and you can start the process at mostlymutts.org or stop by during adoption hours.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• Emotionally rich backstory—lost her owner, raised kittens in foster care, now the last one waiting—delivers instant reader connection
• Independent personality with clear fit criteria makes her highly matchable for the right adult household
• Implied urgency as her kittens have already been adopted, framing Boots as overdue for her own happy ending
